Sample ledger

Counts follow what you choose to generate. Relative populations are not branching fractions or production rates.

What did we measure?

A mass and a resolution

The Gaussian fit maximizes the likelihood of the unbinned values. Its mean estimates the peak position; its width describes the toy response. Parents have fixed masses, so this is not a natural-width measurement.

μ̂ = Σm / N
σ̂² = Σ(m − μ̂)² / N
δμ ≈ σ̂ / √N
More data, smaller error

Fit 100 events, then add 1,000 and fit again. The error on the mean should usually shrink. The peak width should remain similar. The Gaussian is an approximation to the imposed smearing; errors omit systematic uncertainty.

Events are not luminosity

No integrated luminosity is assigned. Converting event counts to luminosity needs a process cross section, branching fraction, acceptance and efficiency: N = ℒ × σprocess × BR × A × ε. None are calibrated here.

Model limitations & primary sources

Phase-space decays conserve four-momentum. No matrix elements, spin correlations, showers, backgrounds, trigger, acceptance selection or calibrated CMS response are simulated. Jets in the new channels are two-hadron cluster proxies with a fixed 5 GeV mass; b labels and W/top combinations come from truth. Display filters do not select the analysis sample. Fits use pure signal and all generated objects, even outside detector acceptance.

CMS: top → Wb and semileptonic tt̄ · CMS: Higgs production and four leptons · CMS: diphotons and forward VBF jets

CMS // FIELD NOTES

A detector, made explorable.

This is a reproducible educational simulation, not real CMS collision data or a live CERN feed. The four-step animation illustrates interpretation; its speed does not represent detector timing or the CMS software pipeline.

Physics audit: what the curves mean

In a uniform +z field, a charged particle follows a constant-radius helix, not an expanding spiral. R = pT / (0.2998 |q/e| B), and the displacement along z per turn is 2π pz / (0.2998 |q/e| B). Default muons have pT ≈ 45.7 GeV/c and R ≈ 40 m. Soft charged hadrons can curl: at pT = 0.6 GeV/c, R ≈ 0.53 m. The orbit centre is displaced from the beam axis.

The corrected r–z view uses nonnegative r = √(x²+y²). The old sign(y) × r convention could jump discontinuously and falsely draw connecting zigzags. A real radial projection can still rise and fall as a helix approaches and recedes from the beam axis.

Trajectories now use exact uniform-field Lorentz steps, with explicit field-boundary intersections. Solid hadron/electron paths stop at the tracker envelope; calorimeter responses remain toy extrapolations. Muons switch to a dashed, straight tangent outside the solenoid. Real CMS has a nonuniform return field; this outer part is not a physically validated muon trajectory. At most one revolution is shown for curling particles. This is a labeled display cutoff, not particle stopping or an energy-loss prediction. Neutral particles do not bend.

Scientific model

Approximate early Run 3 (2022) geometry: Phase-1 pixels, silicon strips, ECAL, HCAL, a 3.8 T solenoid, five barrel yoke wheels with three radial steel layers and four endcap steel disks per side, DT/CSC/RPC muon regions and installed GE1/1 GEM stations. Future HGCAL, MTD, ME0 and full GE2/1 stations are excluded. Small demonstrator modules are omitted. CMS's main envelope is about 21 m × 15 m; forward HCAL extends beyond it.

Charged paths use pT = 0.2998 |q/e| B R within r < 3 m and |z| < 6.25 m. Beyond that volume the muon continuation is a straight tangent: an illustrative approximation, not a return-field simulation. Calorimeter cells, chamber sizes and signals are coarse display geometry, not engineering data.

Two-body and sequential tt̄ / Higgs decays conserve four-momentum before independent toy response smearing. The Higgs four-lepton channel uses one off-shell Z. Production labels identify illustrative topologies; no production rates or spin correlations are predicted. New-channel jets are two-hadron cluster proxies with 5 GeV mass, with truth-known assignments. The Data & fits tab counts unique no-pile-up toy events and offers an approximate Gaussian maximum-likelihood peak fit, not a CMS measurement. Dijet constituents and soft backgrounds are balanced pairs. The 13.6 TeV label supplies LHC context; there is no complete proton collision, parton shower, material interaction, trigger or track-fit simulation. “Reconstructed” values are smeared truth momenta. Jets are sums of generated constituent groups, not a clustering algorithm. Toy resolution constants are not CMS performance claims.

Missing transverse momentum is minus the sum of all reconstructed visible momenta, including pile-up. Filters change presentation only. Neutrinos leave no signals. Photons have dashed neutral flight guides and ECAL deposits, never charged tracks. Truth overlay is dashed. Geometry modes move detector presentation only; hits and particles stay in physical coordinates, so exploded modules do not line up with hits.

Controls

Drag: orbit · right-drag / two fingers: pan · wheel / pinch: zoom.
Space: play / pause · N: next · R: reset · 1–5: camera · C: geometry · L: labels · Escape: clear selection / close. Capture exports the 3D scene. Reduced motion disables automatic playback on load.
